title: Physical Health
body: Check in with how you feel. Movement and regular checkups help you stay well. Ask a peer or clinic if something feels off. To keep a list of medicines you take, use My Health. That list is a memory aid, not medical advice.

articles.title: A checkup when you feel okay
articles.summary: A regular visit can catch problems early.
articles.body: A checkup is a visit when you feel okay, not only when you are sick. The clinic can check blood pressure, ask what medicines you take, and talk about shots. Write down questions before you go. Your own medicine list belongs in My Health. This note is not medical advice.

articles.title: Moving a little each day
articles.body: You do not need a gym. A short walk, light stretching, or standing up more often can help your body. Start with what feels safe. If something hurts or you feel dizzy, stop and ask a doctor or clinic. This note is not a workout plan.

title: Mental Health
summary: Support for your mind and mood.
body: Feeling stressed or low is common. Talking with a peer, counselor, or trusted person can help. Crisis lines are under Help Now.

articles.title: Small ways to care for your mood
articles.summary: Talking with someone you trust can help.
articles.body: Your mood can change from day to day. A regular bedtime, a meal, a short walk, or a talk with a peer can make the day easier. You do not have to handle it alone. This note does not diagnose anything.

articles.title: When to ask for more help
articles.summary: Reach out if daily life stays hard.
articles.body: Ask a clinic, counselor, or peer if you feel low, worried, or numb for many days, or if everyday tasks get hard. If you might hurt yourself, open Help Now. This note does not replace a doctor.

title: Stress Management
summary: Small steps that can take the edge off.
body: These short notes are reading only. You do not have to track this or hit a goal.

articles.title: Everyday ways to ease stress
articles.summary: Small steps can take the edge off.
articles.body: Stress is a normal body response. A few slow breaths, a short walk, or talking with someone you trust can help. You do not have to track this or hit a goal. If stress gets in the way of daily life, talk with a doctor, counselor, or peer.

articles.title: When stress feels like too much
articles.summary: Ask for help if it will not let up.
articles.body: Feeling tense, worried, or worn out for many days is a reason to reach out. A clinic, counselor, or peer can help you sort next steps. If you might hurt yourself, open Help Now. This note does not replace a doctor.

title: Nutrition
body: You do not need a perfect diet. Aim for regular meals when you can, drink water, and ask your clinic about food resources nearby.

articles.title: Eating when you can
articles.summary: Regular meals and water are a fine start.
articles.body: You do not need a perfect diet. Try to eat at regular times, drink water, and add fruit or vegetables when you can get them. If food is hard to afford, ask your clinic or a peer about food help nearby. This note is not a meal plan.

articles.title: A simple way to fill a plate
articles.body: When you can, fill half the plate with fruits and vegetables. Use the rest for grains and protein. Water is a good drink. A clinic can help if diabetes or another condition changes what you eat. This is general information, not a diet made for you.

title: Preventive Care
body: Vaccines and checkups can catch problems early. Ask your clinic which ones are right for you this year.

articles.title: Checks before you feel sick
articles.summary: Ask which tests are due this year.
articles.body: A screening is a check for a problem before you feel sick. Which ones you need depends on your age and health. Ask your clinic what is due this year. This note does not list every test.

articles.title: Shots that protect you
articles.body: Vaccines, also called shots, help your body get ready for some illnesses. Adults need them too, not only children. Ask your clinic which ones fit you. This note does not tell you to get a specific shot.

title: Sleep
body: Sleep stands on its own here. These short notes stay the same for a long time.

articles.title: Everyday sleep tips
articles.summary: A cool, dark room can help.
articles.body: Try to go to bed and wake up around the same time. A cooler, darker, quiet room can make sleep easier. Skip big meals, caffeine, and bright screens close to bedtime when you can. If sleep stays hard, talk with a doctor.

articles.title: Sleep apnea
articles.body: Sleep apnea means breathing stops and starts while you sleep. Loud snoring, gasping, or feeling very tired in the day can be signs. A doctor can check it. This short note is not a diagnosis.
